description_full: MITSUI-SOKO HOLDINGS Co., Ltd., together with its subsidiaries, provides various logistics services in Japan and internationally. The company operates two segments, Logistics Business and Real Estate Business. The Logistics Business segment offers various logistics services, such as warehousing and cargo handling, port operations, transportation, overseas logistics, multimodal transport, air cargo transport, third-party logistics, supply chain management support, and land transportation. The Real Estate Business segment provides building rental services. It also operates container terminals that connect offshore and onshore logistics. In addition, the company offers vessel operations for managing large and heavy cargo, as well as ship agency services that oversee port entry and departure processes, the issuance of bills of lading, and cargo bookings on behalf of shipping companies. The company was formerly known as Mitsui-Soko Co., Ltd. and changed its name to MITSUI-SOKO HOLDINGS Co., Ltd. in October 2014. The company was incorporated in 1909 and is headquartered in Tokyo, Japan.

financial_summary: MITSUI-SOKO HOLDINGS Co., Ltd. is a small-cap industrials business with a $746M market cap on $1.9B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -4% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.

Returns on capital run at 8% against a 7% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically, and 15% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $76M in free cash flow — roughly 4 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.13× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.1× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage of 22× is fortress-like.
Net dilution runs at 2.7% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp.
